sections.h2: What the office does when you sell
sections.html:
A sale in Portage County reaches the public record through one office: the Register of Deeds/Land Description office. It files the deed and collects the state's transfer fee when you hand the deed over. Until staff accept the document, the sale isn't on record. Stevens Point, the largest city and county seat, is where most sellers go.

Wis. Stat. 77.22 tells the register to take the fee on arrival and write the amount across the deed before recording it. Whether your stated price is fair, or your exemption valid, isn't the register's call, so get the figures right before you submit.

The office keeps official records of real estate, personal property and vital statistics. Before you go, ask about hours, accepted payment types and mail submissions.

Recording a typical document costs $30 (s. 59.43(2)(ag)). A sale also owes the transfer fee, 30 cents per $100 of value. Some document types are priced differently, so ask the office for your exact total before you write the check.

ServiceAmount
Recording a document$30
Real estate transfer fee30 cents per $100 of value
Copy of a recorded document$2 first page, $1 each added page
Certification of a copy$1 more
Transfer worth $1,000 or lessNo transfer fee (s. 77.25(13))

Value means everything paid or to be paid, liens included. A land contract is measured by the principal the buyer commits to pay in total. One fifth of every transfer fee stays in the county, and the state receives the remainder (s. 77.24).

The eRETR (electronic real estate transfer return) is a state tax form every conveyance requires. The county's instructions: fill it out online at the state revenue site, print the receipt, then mail or bring the receipt, deed and fees to the Register of Deeds. Section 77.22(1) has grantor and grantee both sign it.

The law makes filing electronic, with a waiver available from the secretary of revenue only after a written hardship application. The register can't take a deed lacking a finished return and the fee. Usually the title company or closing attorney files it; as seller, compare the price shown with your purchase contract.

  • Price plus any liens the buyer takes on makes up the value.
  • Because both sides are named, collect the buyer's details early.
  • Keep the receipt stapled to the original deed until the recorded copy comes back.

Some conveyances owe nothing under s. 77.25, and an exempt deed carries the subsection number on its face. Courts read exemptions tightly, so a case that merely resembles one should be treated as taxable until a title professional advises otherwise.

  • An inherited house passing under a will, by descent or by survivorship (s. 77.25(11)).
  • Handing a house to a child, stepchild or grandchild for little or nothing (s. 77.25(8)).
  • A lender or land contract seller taking title in foreclosure or by deed in lieu (s. 77.25(14)).
  • A deed that fixes or confirms an earlier recorded conveyance, with nominal or no consideration (s. 77.25(3)).
  • Delinquent tax or assessment sales (s. 77.25(4)).

Local governments may not add a fee to a conveyance the state exempts (s. 77.256), and s. 77.255 says when an exempt transfer needs no return.

Documents that stray from the layout in s. 59.43(2m) can be refused. Place the title anywhere from half an inch to six inches down page one. Keep an empty 3 inch by 3 inch box in the page's top right corner, within the margins, for recording information; without it the deed may not be recorded.

Old forms and online templates often miss these points, which is why such deeds come back. Have your title company or attorney read the final deed before signing.

Most real estate tax goes to the County Treasurer at 1516 Church Street, Stevens Point, (715) 346-1348, open weekdays 7:30 am to 4:30 pm. Installments are due January 31 and July 31, and the treasurer covers 23 of 28 municipalities for the first and 27 of 28 for the second. Stevens Point runs its own three installments, so city sellers pay the city. Almond, Belmont and Lanark (towns) and Milladore (village) keep their first installment local. Request an exact payoff from the right treasurer before closing.

  • Paying by check or cash, at the window or by mail, is free.
  • Vendor fees apply otherwise: 2.39 percent on credit cards, $3.95 for online debit, $1.50 per electronic check.
  • Expect no reminder before the second installment. Late taxes get no payment plan, although partial payments are taken.

Miss an installment and you lose the right to pay in installments; interest of 1.5 percent a month then builds on what's unpaid. The sixth business day after the due date is when delinquency starts, since s. 74.11(7) and (8) give five working days of grace.

A balance open on September 1 leads the county to issue a tax certificate and mail notice of it. Two years remain to pay that year's tax before tax deed foreclosure starts. Auctions are listed on the county's Tax Deed Land Sale page.

Behind on taxes? The county names the Foundation for Rural Housing as a possible source of funds for delinquent taxes: 608-238-3448 or 888-400-5974.

Look for three credits on the bill. Every bill gets the school levy tax credit, and parcels with an improvement get the first dollar credit, both without any action from you. The lottery and gaming credit is different: it covers a primary residence, requires a claim, and applies to one parcel only. The Treasurer's page posts ratios, credits and mill rates for 2021 through 2025.

Land records live at landinfo.co.portage.wi.gov, the same site the Treasurer uses for tax lookups and online payments. Type the parcel number by itself in the bill's format, because added terms shrink results. You can also try a property address or a first and last name.

Check the parcel record before listing: owner, mailing address and tax status should all agree with the deed you intend to sign.

Recording works the same for a cash buyer. The closing agent drafts the deed, files the eRETR naming both parties and forwards receipt, deed and fees. The buyer has no mortgage to record, though a satisfaction for any loan you're paying off still is. Ask which exemption, if any, fits, and confirm unpaid taxes come out of your proceeds.

The 2020 count was 70,377 people, and the 2025 estimate is 71,943. About 68.4 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. Twenty-eight municipalities, from the City of Stevens Point to small towns like Alban, Hull and New Hope, all file deeds at this one office, but each decides who collects its first tax installment.

faqs.a: To the Register of Deeds/Land Description office. Submit the signed deed, eRETR receipt and fees as one packet, and call ahead about hours and payment types.

faqs.q: How big is the transfer fee?
faqs.a: It's 30 cents per $100 of value (Wis. Stat. 77.22(1)), the seller's cost, in addition to $30 for recording.
Yes, unless the transfer is exempt. Finish it on the state's revenue site, print the receipt, and give it to the register along with the deed.
Not for the inheritance itself, which s. 77.25(11) exempts. A later sale by the heir is a fresh conveyance and does owe the fee.
First installment January 31, second July 31. The city of Stevens Point and a few towns and a village collect locally, so read your bill's coupons.
